Splitting the Housework Fairly

For a household where the work is not landing evenly. It gets every task written down including the invisible ones, hands over ownership rather than help, trades by dread as much as minutes, and sets the standard out loud once.

Chores · Relationships · Communication · Boundaries · 9 items · once a week

The checklist

  • Write down every task, including the invisible ones — remembering is work and belongs on the list.
  • Pick who owns a task rather than who helps with it — owning means noticing it, not being asked.
  • Stop asking to be asked — a job you have to request is still your job.
  • Trade by how much you hate it, not by minutes — fairness is about dread as much as time.
  • Set the standard out loud once — half of these arguments are two definitions of clean.
  • Let them do it their way once it is theirs — redoing it silently is how ownership dies.
  • Put the weekly reset in the calendar — a named hour beats waiting for somebody to crack.
  • Review the split every few months — jobs and babies and seasons change what is fair.
  • Pay for one thing if you can afford to — an hour of help is cheaper than the resentment.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it once a week, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
